name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Oregon dairy-linked case 19 Nov; 4 US since Oct
summary: Oregon's mild dairy-linked H5 case on 19 Nov is the fourth US case since mid-Oct; no human-to-human spread
state: Oregon Health Authority confirmed on 19 Nov the state's first human H5 case of 2026, a person with mild symptoms linked to a Morrow County dairy outbreak, and said the virus is not known to spread between people (OHA). ECDC's 3 Nov update recorded three dairy-linked cases in Yakima County, Washington, since 15 Oct, one fatal, all tied to animal exposure (ECDC). No new human case was found from 20 to 23 Nov. Cases remain sporadic and animal-linked, so Normal holds; the trend is rising.
for_you: Officials rate the risk to the public as low. People who work with dairy cattle or poultry are most exposed; UKHSA and CDC advise avoiding contact with sick or dead birds and animals and reporting them to the authorities.
rubric_hit: Sporadic animal-to-human cases only (4 US dairy-linked since 15 Oct); no cluster or human-to-human spread

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
